summary: One goal-scoped requirement preserves existing missing-person cases and area-watch consequences in headless JSON debriefs. Completion requires current code inspection and behavioral verification; no implementation gap is inferred from the code index.

requirements.title: Preserve existing case and area-watch consequences in JSON debriefs
requirements.quote: | missing persons and cases [S] | each open case; the area watch: +1 posted guard and +1 camera on the block where the person was last seen, for 3 missions; the district's security level S | a kill never found: +2 T, no Menace, close ties fear +1, the case stays open until the body is found · a found killing: −1 Standing, grief, its case closes after 3 missions · every 2 open cases raise S by 1, at most +2 |
acceptance: Inspect the current consequence model, debrief construction, JSON writer and relevant consumers/tests to establish the existing behavior and wire contract before identifying any serialization gap; index entries and prior reviews are not completion evidence.

For existing simulation results containing missing-person cases, parsed headless JSON preserves each case and its available consequence data, including area-watch location, added guard and camera, duration, and district security consequence. Values come from existing computed results, without recalculation or invented fields or rules.

Verify that existing results retain the §08 semantics where represented: an unfound killing remains an open case until discovery; area watch adds one posted guard and one camera on the last-seen block for three missions; a found killing's case closes after three missions; each two open cases contribute one security level, capped at a contribution of two. Missing or conflicting rulebook definitions are inspection blockers, not authorization to implement new consequences.
Repeated serialization of the same completed result produces identical JSON. Replaying the same start state and orders produces equivalent case and area-watch debrief data.
Constructing or serializing the debrief does not mutate simulation state, checksums, case lifetimes, consequence totals or subsequent results, and does not apply any consequence a second time.

Preserve established JSON fields, types and values and existing consumer behavior. Verify backward compatibility for results with no cases or area watch as well as populated results; determine absent-versus-empty conventions from the current contract rather than inventing them.
Do not introduce campaign persistence, advance the campaign, or change Trail, Standing, fear, security or case-generation rules to satisfy serialization checks.
requirements.rationale: Preserves consequential simulation output at a narrow shared-library boundary. Expected implementation effort is modest, but omissions, accidental consequence reapplication and wire-contract changes warrant focused verification. Source: §08, passage 55c5c6cd533522c040aca4a6; replay constraints: §09 human passage 0dffd14eab5f60ca398c8382 and §11. Side-effect freedom and backward compatibility are explicit goal constraints. Scores are provisional pending current code inspection.
